This course is being brought to you by University Malaysia Sabah in collaboration with the Commonwealth
Biological agents pose a significant threat to public health and safety.
Biological agents include bacteria, viruses and other pathogens, which have the potential
to cause harm to healthy human subjects.
BioRisk Management involves three basic steps.
The first step is Risk Assessment.
The BioSafety officer assesses the risk posed by the pathogen to the laboratory users using
The next step of the procedure involves Risk Mitigation.
Risk Mitigation involves the application of the five controls to mitigate or reduce
the risk posed by a biological agent.
Finally, we move on to Performance Assessment.
Performance Assessment determines whether the controls are appropriate and in proper working
These three steps constitute the process of BioRisk Management.
Thank you for watching and stay bio safe.
